1. Heard Sri Ashok Kumar Srivastava "Ratan", learned counsel for the appellant and Sri Satya Narayan Gupta, learned counsel for the claimant-respondent nos. 1 and 2.
No one is present on behalf of respondent nos. 3 and 4, who are driver and owner of Pickup vehicle.

2. This first appeal from order has been filed by the appellant-Insurance Company against the judgement and award dated 06.11.2013 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal/ Additional District Judge/ Special Judge (E.C. Act) in C.P. No. 78 of 2011 (Dayaram and another Vs. Naval Kishor and others) by which compensation of Rs. 3,13,000/- along with 7% interest has been awarded in favour of claimants-respondents and liability has been fixed upon the The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Dayaram And 3 Others on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123947718/
1 appellant-Insurance Company on account of death of Raju @ Satole aged about 25 years.
3.

sentences.text: It is submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that it was a case of head on collision in between motorcycle and Pickup vehicle.
The Pickup vehicle was insured with the appellant-Insurance Company.
The accident was occurred on account of sole negligence of motorcyclist and there was no negligence on the part of driver of insured vehicle.
It is further submitted that in any case it was a case of head on collision in between motorcycle and insured vehicle and both the vehicles were equally negligent and responsible for the accident.
The claims tribunal has erred in deciding issue no.1 holding sole negligence of driver of insured vehicle and nothing has been deducted in terms of contributory negligence of motorcyclist.
No other ground has been pressed by the learned counsel for the appellant.

4. On the other hand, learned appearing on behalf of claimants-respondents submits that admittedly the deceased was pillion rider of motorcycle bearing number U.P. 94 C 5675, which was driven by one Narendra Bangali.
It is further submitted that there was no contribution of deceased towards accident.
The claims tribunal has rightly fixed entire liability upon the appellant being insurer of offending vehicle.

5. Considered the submissions of learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.
Admittedly, the deceased Raju @ Satole was pillion rider of motorcycle bearing number U.P. 94 C 5675, which was driven by one Narendra Bangali.

The claims tribunal after considering the entire evidence and material which are available on record has recorded finding while deciding issue no.1 that the driver of insured vehicle was rash and negligent and was responsible for the accident.
The finding recorded y the claims tribunal in respect of negligence is based on evidence and there is no illegality in any manner.

Even otherwise the law has been settled by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Khenyei vs New India Assurnace Co.Ltd. & Ors reported in 2015 (9) SCC 273 that in case of composite negligence it is open to the claimant to claim compensation either from both the vehicles or from one vehicle.

entities.text: Khenyei vs New India Assurnace Co.Ltd. & Ors reported in 2015 (9) SCC 273
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. The present claim petition has been filed by claimants claiming compensation from the owner and insurer of insured vehicle.

Since the deceased was pillion rider of motorcycle and there was no contribution of the deceased in the accident and it was a case of composite negligence, the claims tribunal has rightly fixed the entire liability upon the appellant-Insurance Company being insurer of Pickup vehicle.
8. No ground for interference is made out.
The first appeal from order is devoid of merits and is accordingly dismissed.
9. Interim order, if any, stands discharged.
